methods.label: Compare equal parts of each square
methods.explanation:
The midpoint condition suggests dividing each large square into four equal smaller squares. Draw the horizontal and vertical lines through opposite side midpoints wherever they are missing. Each smaller square has one-fourth the area of a large square.

In \(I\), the sloping diagonal cuts two of the smaller squares in half. One half of each is shaded, so the shaded total is
\[
\frac12\cdot\frac14+\frac12\cdot\frac14=\frac14
\]
of the large square.

In \(II\), exactly one of the four smaller squares is shaded, again giving \(\frac14\) of the large square.

In \(III\), the existing sloping segments form both diagonals of each smaller square. These diagonals divide a smaller square into four equal-area triangles: their bases are the four equal sides, and their heights are all half a side because the diagonals meet at the center. Exactly one of these triangles is shaded in each smaller square. The shaded total is therefore one-fourth of all four smaller squares together, or \(\frac14\) of the large square.

Since the large squares are the same size, all three shaded areas are equal, choice \(\boxed{\mathrm{A}}\).
methods.levelReason: The comparison uses elementary square partitions, the base-height meaning of triangle area, and simple fractions. It requires no similarity or advanced quadrilateral theorem.
